raw_response:
My land is 9 mu. Cotton is my main crop — been growing it for most of my 20 years. It is how I pay for school fees and household expenses. Maize I keep for food and to sell what is left over. Mungbean I plant on a small piece because it sells fast in summer and does not need much work.

Some of my family work in town, so I cannot rely on them during peak cotton season. I have to plan carefully with my own hands and maybe hire day labor during harvest. Cotton takes the most land and most of my attention — I give it 5 mu. Maize gets 3 mu. Mungbean gets the last 1 mu.

For seeds, I use improved cotton — the Bt varieties. Everyone in the village does now. Bollworm used to ruin us before. For maize, I buy hybrid seed from the county supply store every year, same as always. For mungbean, I save my own seed from last year.

Fertilizer I apply how I was taught and how I see my neighbors do it. Cotton needs the most, especially nitrogen during boll filling. Maize also needs good nitrogen. Mungbean I do not push hard — it fixes some nitrogen itself and I do not want to waste money on it.

I have my well and the pump. I irrigate cotton 4 times — at germination, squaring, peak boll, and once more if it is dry in August. Maize I irrigate 3 times. Mungbean 2 times is usually enough.

Pesticides for cotton I still spray 6 times — mostly for aphids, spider mites, and whitefly. Bollworm is less of a problem now with the Bt variety. Maize I spray 2 times. Mungbean 2 times for pod borer and aphids.

I plough cotton fields in spring before planting. For maize and mungbean, rotary tillage is faster and saves time.
